task_specification.objective: Deliver three bounded tasks for camera/HUD readability, authored arena and boss spatial integrity, and dense-run resilience/evidence readiness while preserving the authored cemetery package, fixed upgrade slots, and existing build behavior.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release convergence is blocked by an unbounded cemetery world edge, landmark/Bellkeeper camera occlusion, and an outcome-unknown dense-profile Godot MCP timeout. The repair must restore authored-world bindings and isolate dense qualification readiness from renderer-dependent verdicts.

stop_conditions: Do not replace, hide, duplicate, extract, or surgically edit the preserved authored cemetery package.
Do not infer dense qualification from llvmpipe, counters, or diagnostics without a completed renderer-gated host sample.
Stop after the three scoped implementation tasks and their Tester/host recapture criteria are defined.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different root-cause approach from prior transform tuning: repair camera/HUD event ownership, restore gameplay bindings to the intact authored environment with explicit collision and occlusion-safe encounter anchors, and isolate dense-run reset/performance instrumentation behind release guards.

code: Run native Godot boot and integrity checks plus focused parse/load checks for every modified scene, script, resource, and UI file.
Exercise start, advance, reset, and retry twice to detect duplicate signals, stale singleton state, orphan enemies, and unreleased deferred work.
Verify the authored cemetery remains a single intact instance and no replacement floor, road, facade, landmark-pack, or duplicated environment assets were introduced.
runtime: Tester/host recapture release_convergence_camera_movement_dash_contract with real horizontal yaw and vertical pitch probes, full-screen HUD mouse_filter inspection, dash/movement replay, and keyboard/mouse/gamepad choice focus checks.

Tester/host recapture release_convergence_wave_director_boss_contract from spawn through the ordinary wave route, Bellkeeper activation, landmark approach/departure, perimeter collision replay, and terminal/result transition.
Tester/host request the Godot MCP rebind and run a renderer-gated dense profile using timing/population/reset receipts; capture a bounded sample before and after reset and retain raw runtime logs.
visual: Compare same-framing spawn, critical-route, landmark, and four cardinal interior-street views before and after repair; reject black void, proxy-floor takeover, landmark disappearance, or Bellkeeper occlusion.

Inspect the shipped HUD and upgrade draft at native viewport, fullscreen, and windowed scales; reject text-stacked choices, missing silhouettes/icons, placeholder CURRENT values, more than three decision deltas, or incomplete focus states.
Confirm cemetery lighting, materials, streets, buildings, and props remain grounded and coherent with the bound gameplay reference.

done_when: Movement is camera-relative on the arena plane; a real horizontal mouse probe changes yaw and camera_forward, and a vertical probe changes pitch.

The choice hierarchy uses authored visual hierarchy with weapon/upgrade silhouettes or icons, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states.
Held confirm is debounced, fixed card dimensions remain stable, and full-screen HUD mouse filtering does not capture or suppress the required movement probes.
tasks.instructions: Repair camera/input ownership and the player-facing choice hierarchy as one readability surface. Keep the camera gently tracking and expose approach lanes, threats, pickups, and movement-direction space without dense-combat occlusion. Audit input routing and full-screen HUD mouse_filter behavior so horizontal and vertical mouse motion produce measurable yaw/pitch changes. Implement the required visual hierarchy: lead each weapon or upgrade choice with authored silhouettes or icons, use compact stat icons, show truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, omit unchanged or placeholder rows, and provide keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, hover, unavailable, and selected states. Preserve existing upgrade transaction semantics and fixed card slots.
tasks.title: Repair camera-relative movement and visual choice hierarchy

done_when: The intact authored cemetery remains one native visual environment instance, with only an outer datum plus additive gameplay collision, navigation, spawn, and objective anchors.

The arena has expand or larger traversable scale, coherent external world or external depth beyond the boundary/perimeter, and a visible central building or landmark that remains stable under ordinary movement or movement replay.
Prominent approaches and the full boundary/perimeter have aligned collision; traversal shows no pass-through, disappearance, or occlusion of the player, Bellkeeper, or landmark.

Bellkeeper encounter framing keeps the active boss visible before approach, at near contact, and after departure, while the ordinary wave director remains bounded and reaches its declared boss/result transitions exactly once.
Four cardinal first-person views from an interior native street plus spawn and critical-route views show no black void or proxy-floor takeover.
tasks.instructions: Restore the authored cemetery integration without replacing the package. Rebase player spawn, navigation, objective anchors, and gameplay boundary/perimeter onto native streets or terrain; remove or minimize unrelated proxy/support clutter. Expand to a larger traversable scale with coherent external world/external depth beyond the playable perimeter. Treat the central building/landmark as gameplay geometry: align its collision, navigation exclusion, spawn safety, and camera handling; use bounded transparency or selective facade/roof handling instead of whole-landmark hiding. Reposition Bellkeeper encounter anchors and camera framing so ordinary movement, dash, and movement replay cannot cause disappearance or occlusion. Preserve the authored child hierarchy and native materials, streets, buildings, and props.
tasks.title: Restore authored cemetery boundary, collision, and boss framing

done_when: A dense-profile run can start, advance, reset, and replay through authoritative gameplay APIs without hangs, duplicate signals, stale references, or orphaned enemies.
Release-guarded diagnostics expose deterministic wave state, active/spawned enemy counts, spawn cadence, frame-time or tick budget, and reset-generation receipts for host capture.

Pooling or lifecycle reset clears health, targets, velocity, timers, status effects, animation, collision, visibility, signals, and deferred work; runtime logs show no new errors or timeout loops in a bounded dense window.
Diagnostics do not alter release gameplay semantics, and native dense qualification remains renderer-gated rather than being declared from instrumentation alone.
tasks.instructions: Harden dense-profile execution and make the blocked Godot MCP path retestable. Audit wave-director scheduling, enemy pooling/lifecycle, spawn throttles, and restart/reset ownership for unbounded work or stale references that can produce outcome-unknown timeouts. Add candidate-owned release-guarded telemetry for timing, population, cadence, wave/boss state, and reset generation, with explicit start/advance/reset receipts and no release-export tester shortcuts. Keep the native dense gap renderer-gated; diagnostics enable host recapture but never substitute for it.
tasks.title: Make dense runs bounded, reset-safe, and measurable
